Relaxation of a symmetric viscous layer (s=Δρgh0​κ/[2μ(λ+2κ)])

Words: 135 Articles: 1
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
A layer of half-thickness h0​, dynamic viscosity μ and density ρ, between semi-infinite fluids of viscosity λμ and densities ρ∓Δρ, relaxes a symmetric thickness Fourier mode. In the plug-like extensional viscosity regime, mass conservation and 4μ(hux​)x​=hΔρghx​−σxz+​ together with the Fourier traction map for a viscous half-space give the displayed rate, where κ=∣k∣h0​. Inner longitudinal extension dominates for λ≪κ; outer tangential resistance dominates for κ≪λ while the plug approximation remains valid.

Uniform high-viscosity limit of viscous-layer relaxation (s∼2μΔρgh0​​1+(2/3)λκ3(2/3)κ2​)

Words: 73
Relaxation of a symmetric viscous layer OurBigBook.com
For κ≪1 and λκ≫1, the displayed formula retains both inner transverse shear stress and outer normal-velocity resistance. When κ−1≪λ≪κ−3, almost immobile tangential interfaces create a pressure-driven parabolic flow and s∼Δρgh0​κ2/(3μ). When λκ3≫1, the exterior's normal viscous dissipation dominates and s∼Δρg/(2λμ∣k∣). The exact symmetric three-layer Stokes flow dispersion relation is
s=2μκΔρgh0​​λcosh(2κ)+(sinhκcoshκ+κ)+λ2(sinhκcoshκ−κ)sinh2κ+λ(sinhκcoshκ−κ)​.
(1)
The term proportional to λ2κ3 in its denominator prevents extrapolating a fixed-λ long-wave expansion uniformly to every large-λ scaling.

Fourier traction map for a viscous half-space (σxy​=−2μ∣k∣U,σyy​=−2μ∣k∣V)

Words: 73
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
For a two-dimensional decaying Stokes flow in y>0, prescribe boundary Fourier mode (U,V)eikx. The boundary shear stress and normal stress are the displayed diagonal map, with the common exponential understood. For k>0 and V=0, the Unscaled Papkovich–Neuber representation gives u=U(1−ky)eikx−ky, v=−ikUyeikx−ky and p=−2iμkUeikx−ky. Differentiation proves the tangential traction and vanishing normal stress. The normal-velocity calculation supplies the second diagonal entry. The map converts a viscous exterior into a nonlocal boundary resistance proportional to ∣k∣.

Stokes far-field multipoles of a deforming body (u=JF+(G×y)/(8πμr3)+Qy/(4πr3)−3(y⋅Sy)y/(8πμr5)+O(r−3))

Words: 72
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
With body-outward normal n, put F=−∫σndS, Σij​=∫xi​(σn)j​dS, Uij​=∫ui​nj​dS, and M=Σ−2μU. Taylor expansion of the exterior boundary integral representation of Stokes flow gives a Stokeslet from F, a rotlet from Gj​=−ϵjkl​Σkl​, a source from Q=TrU, and a stresslet from S=(M+MT)/2−ITrM/3. Thus F and G are the force and torque exerted on the fluid, while Q is the instantaneous displaced-volume rate. A volume-preserving deforming body has Q=0.

Mutual drag reduction of two distant translating spheres (D⊥​/D0​=1−3a/(4b),D∥​/D0​=1−3a/(2b))

Words: 82
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
Two identical radius-a spheres moving together through a viscous fluid at separation b≫a entrain each other. The leading far velocity of one sphere at the other is 3aU/(4b) for separation perpendicular to the velocity, and 3aU/(2b) for parallel separation. Replacing U by its velocity relative to this induced flow in Stokes law gives the displayed drag reductions relative to D0​=6πμaU, with errors of order (a/b)2. Reflection symmetry and linearity imply equal drag on the two spheres in either geometry.

Oseen approximation (ρU⋅∇u=−∇p+μ∇2u)

Words: 178 Articles: 1
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
The Oseen approximation retains advection of a small disturbance by a uniform incident velocity U, but neglects advection of the disturbance by itself. Its steady equations are
ρ(U⋅∇)u=−∇p+μ∇2u,∇⋅u=0.
(2)
A Stokes disturbance of a sphere decays as Ua/r, so the ratio of background advection to viscous diffusion grows as Ur/ν. Thus the approximation resolves the outer region r∼ν/U, where the Stokes flow expansion is nonuniform, while self-convection remains smaller by a/r.

Potential-source and wake decomposition of sphere Oseen flow (ϕ=−3aν/(2r),χ=3ae(U⋅x−Ur)/(2ν)/(2r))

Words: 107
Oseen approximation OurBigBook.com
Let U=∣U∣, ν=μ/ρ, and r=∣x∣. A decaying outer disturbance matched to the leading translating sphere in Stokes flow is
ϕ=−2r3aν​,χ=2r3a​exp[2νU⋅x−Ur​],u=∇ϕ+ν∇χ−Uχ.
(3)
Here Δϕ=0 and (νΔ−U⋅∇)χ=0 away from zero. The substitution χ=heU⋅x/(2ν) reduces the latter equation to (Δ−U2/(4ν2))h=0, whose decaying radial solution is proportional to e−Ur/(2ν)/r. In the inner overlap, cancellation of the potential monopole gives u∼−3a[U+n(U⋅n)]/(4r). The potential source's volume flux is 6πνa, and its mass flux is 6πμa. Downstream, the fluid wake width grows as νx/U​; its mass deficit balances this source, while its momentum deficit is 6πμaU, the Stokes drag law.

Cylinder in a simple shear Stokes flow

Words: 51
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
For a stationary cylinder of radius a in the far-field shear (Γy,0), the stream function is ψ=(Γ/4)[r2−2a2log(r/a)−a2−(r2−2a2+a4/r2)cos2φ]. It solves the biharmonic equation and the no-slip boundary condition. The fluid exerts torque −2πμΓa2 per unit length, because the angular part of the surface traction averages to zero and the mean tangential traction is −μΓ.

Zero total flux for localized tube Stokes flow (Qf​(z)=−Vz​As​(z))

Words: 82
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
Extend the velocity rigidly through a moving sphere in an incompressible tube flow. The extended velocity is continuous and divergence-free, so its total flux is independent of height. Quiescent far-field conditions make this flux zero. The sphere contributes Vz​As​ through a cross-section; the rotational contribution integrates to zero over its circular slice. Thus the fluid flux compensates the solid displacement. A descending sphere generates upward fluid flux in every section cutting its interior. This statement assumes a localized flow with no imposed throughflow and negligible tube-end effects.

Surface independence of Stokes force and torque integrals (∫S​σndS,∫S​x×σndS)

Words: 77
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
For Stokes flow without body forces, ∇⋅σ=0. Symmetry of the Newtonian fluid stress tensor also gives ∇⋅(x×σ)=0, interpreted componentwise as the angular-momentum flux. The divergence theorem makes the resultant force and torque the same on any two homologous enclosing surfaces lying in a nonsingular fluid region. In a boundary perturbation of a nearly spherical particle, evaluating each perturbation field on a fixed enclosing surface avoids spurious geometric force terms: the geometric terms from changing the surface normal and area cancel those from evaluating the base stress at the displaced surface.

Brinkman equation (−∇p+μ∇2u=μα2(u−um​))

Words: 101 Articles: 1
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
The Brinkman equation augments Stokes flow with a local drag against a background matrix of velocity um​. The inverse screening length α has units of inverse length. With equal viscous coefficients the permeability is α−2. Taking the curl produces a screened vorticity equation.

Matrix-relative Brinkman velocity

Words: 59
Brinkman equation OurBigBook.com
Porous-matrix drag depends on fluid velocity relative to the matrix, so it is not invariant under adding a uniform fluid velocity while leaving the matrix fixed. In a swimmer frame with stationary laboratory matrix, the drag is proportional to u−Uex​. A constant shift can alternatively be absorbed into a linear pressure term, whose physical interpretation must then be retained.

Viscous buoyant conduit

Words: 176 Articles: 2
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
A slender low-viscosity fluid column inside a much more viscous fluid rises under a density contrast. At negligible inertia, its axial flux is approximately q=πa4(Δρg−Pi,z​)/(8μi​). Radial expansion strains the outer fluid and gives the normal-stress pressure difference Pi​−Po​=2μo​at​/a at leading order when inner normal viscous stress and interfacial tension are negligible. Coupling that pressure to volume conservation yields the conduit equation. This two-fluid viscous model differs from a turbulent entraining thermal plume.

Conduit equation (AT​+(A2[1−(AT​/A)Z​])Z​=0)

Words: 103 Articles: 1
Viscous buoyant conduit OurBigBook.com
The conduit equation evolves the positive cross-sectional area A of a viscous buoyant conduit. Its scaling uses axial length a0​/8λ​ and velocity Δρga02​/(8λμo​), where λ=μi​/μo​. Linearization at A=1 gives ω=2k/(1+k2): phase velocity is upward but group velocity changes sign at ∣k∣=1. Nonlinear elevation waves obey the solitary-wave amplitude-speed relation for the conduit equation.

Solitary-wave amplitude-speed relation for the conduit equation (c/f0​=(2lnα−1+α−2)/(1−2/α+α−2))

Words: 58
Conduit equation OurBigBook.com
A positive travelling wave f on a uniform background f0​ has first integral cf′2/(2f2)+V(f)=V(f0​), with V(f)=lnf+c/f+(f02​−cf0​)/(2f2). Equating the crest and background potentials gives the displayed speed relation for crest ratio α>1. The elevation-wave speed exceeds 2f0​ and approaches that long-wave speed as α→1. The formula requires the positive-area branch, rather than continuation through f=0.

Hydrodynamic interaction

Words: 351 Articles: 6
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
Bodies immersed in one fluid affect each other through the flow that each produces. At large separation, a force-driven sphere generates a Stokeslet that modifies the other sphere's velocity. These interactions produce off-diagonal entries in the hydrodynamic mobility matrix.

Stresslet reflection between two force-free and forced spheres

Words: 149 Articles: 1
Hydrodynamic interaction OurBigBook.com
Consider two widely separated rigid spheres of equal radius a, with separation Rn, in Stokes flow. Apply a force 6πμaU0​ to the first sphere and let the second be force-free and torque-free. The second sphere samples the rate-of-strain tensor of the first sphere's Stokeslet, E=3a(U0​⋅n)(I−3nn)/(4R2). Its leading disturbance is the stresslet of a sphere in a uniform straining Stokes flow. Evaluating that disturbance back at the first sphere gives
ΔU=−415​(Ra​)4(U0​⋅n)n.
(4)
The hydrodynamic mobility matrix decreases at fixed force, consistently with the increase of resistance caused by an additional rigid inclusion.

Rotation-clamped reflection between two spheres

Words: 60
Stresslet reflection between two force-free and forced spheres OurBigBook.com
If the otherwise force-free second sphere is held against rotation, its angular velocity relative to the incident fluid is −3a(U0​×n)/(4R2). The rotlet reflected back to the first sphere adds
ΔUrot​=−43​(Ra​)4[U0​−(U0​⋅n)n].
(5)
This follows by evaluating the rotating sphere in Stokes flow at displacement −Rn and using the vector triple-product identity. The holding couple does no work because the held sphere's angular velocity is zero.

Externally driven two-sphere pump

Words: 130 Articles: 2
Hydrodynamic interaction OurBigBook.com
Two spheres whose prescribed translations have a phase lag can exert a nonzero mean force on the fluid while each returns to its starting position. Their changing separation correlates the interaction strength with the other sphere's velocity. This pump is externally driven, so it is distinct from force-free swimming governed by the scallop theorem.

Minimum separation of phase-shifted sphere oscillations (ℓmin​=ℓ0​−2δ∣sin(ϕ/2)∣)

Externally driven two-sphere pump OurBigBook.com
The centre separation for equal-amplitude oscillations has minimum ℓ0​−2δ∣sin(ϕ/2)∣. A bound ℓ0​≥δ alone cannot guarantee nonoverlap. An asymptotic mobility calculation needs this minimum much larger than the sphere radii.

Phase-dependent mean force of an externally driven sphere pair (⟨F1​+F2​⟩t​∼9πμa1​a2​δ2ωℓ0−2​sinϕ)

Words: 48
Externally driven two-sphere pump OurBigBook.com
For equal oscillation amplitudes δ, frequency ω, mean separation ℓ0​ and phase lag ϕ, the leading mean total force on the fluid is 9πμa1​a2​δ2ωsinϕ/ℓ02​. Each sphere supplies half. The large-separation calculation expands the Stokeslet interaction; reciprocal in-phase and antiphase motions have zero mean force.

Longitudinal two-sphere mobility (M=(m1​h​hm2​​))

Words: 36
Hydrodynamic interaction OurBigBook.com
For well-separated spheres moving along their line of centres, the leading mobility matrix has diagonal entries mi​=(6πμai​)−1 and off-diagonal entries h=(4πμℓ)−1. This is the axial Stokeslet interaction. Finite-size and repeated-reflection corrections enter at higher order.

Particle stresslet tensor (S=−sym∫A​x(σn)dS)

Words: 50
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
The symmetric first moment of the traction exerted by a rigid inclusion, with the surface normal pointing into the inclusion. Its contraction with the background rate-of-strain tensor is the strain-related contribution to extra dissipation due to a rigid inclusion. A trace-free version is equivalent for an incompressible flow. This tensor is distinct from the axisymmetric force-dipole flow used as a far-field singularity.

Sphere in a uniform straining Stokes flow

Words: 140 Articles: 1
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
Let the ambient velocity be Ex, with E symmetric and trace free, and centre a rigid sphere of radius a at the origin. It is force-free and torque-free, with zero translation and rotation. Its disturbance is
u′=−r5a5​Ex−2r55a3​(1−r2a2​)(E:xx)x,p′=−r55μa3​(E:xx).
(6)
The total velocity vanishes at r=a, and the leading disturbance is a stresslet. Harmonic dipole and quadrupole potentials in the Papkovich–Neuber representation give the complete field.

Papkovich potentials for a strained sphere (Φ=−5a3Ex/(3r3),χ=a5(x⋅Ex)/r5)

Words: 60
Sphere in a uniform straining Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
With symmetric traceless strain E, these harmonic potentials solve the decaying disturbance around a stationary sphere in the convention u=Φ−21​∇(x⋅Φ+χ) and p=−μ∇⋅Φ. The vector potential supplies the leading stresslet; the scalar degree-two potential corrects no slip at finite radius. Matching the independent Ex and (x⋅Ex)x structures fixes both coefficients.

Linearity of Stokes flow

Words: 26
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
The Stokes equation is linear in velocity, pressure, body force, and boundary data. Solutions may therefore be superposed, and rigid-body velocities depend linearly on applied forces and torques.

Uniqueness of Stokes flow

Words: 45
Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
With prescribed velocity on the boundary and suitable decay or far-field data, a Stokes flow is unique up to an additive pressure constant. Applying the viscous dissipation identity to the difference of two solutions makes its rate-of-strain tensor vanish; the homogeneous boundary data then eliminate the remaining rigid motion.

Stokes flow OurBigBook.com
Let a viscous layer occupy 0<y<h(t), with no slip at y=0, zero tangential traction at y=h, and exterior pressure p0​−ρa​E2x2/2. The Cartesian streamfunction ansatz ψ=xf(y) reduces the Stokes equations to f(4)=0. The resulting surface velocity is
h˙=−3μρa​E2​h3,
(8)
so the positive thinning rate is −h˙=ρa​E2h3/(3μ).

No-slip image system of a normal Stokeslet (S=−2Fd(nn−I/3),M=Fd2n/μ)

Words: 87
Stokeslet OurBigBook.com
A normal point force Fn at height d above a plane with a no-slip boundary condition is balanced by an image Stokeslet −Fn, a stresslet of tensor strength S, and a source dipole of moment M at the reflected point. Here the stresslet convention is ui​=−Sjk​∂k​Gij​, with G the free-space Stokes tensor. Substitution on the plane cancels both normal and tangential velocity. The original and image forces cancel their r−1 terms, while the image stresslet cancels the remaining r−2 force-dipole term; the generic fixed-angle far field is O(r−3).

Stress-free image of a normal Stokeslet

Words: 120
Stokeslet OurBigBook.com
Place a normal Stokeslet below a plane and an equal, oppositely directed image at the reflected point above it. The normal velocity of their sum is odd across the plane and the tangential velocity is even. The plane therefore has zero normal velocity and zero normal derivative of tangential velocity, giving zero tangential stress. For a sphere of radius a translating towards that plane at speed U from distance d≫a, the leading radial surface flow is 3aUrd/[2(r2+d2)3/2], directed outward. The image's incident flow at the sphere changes its required force by relative order a/d, so the first correction to surface velocity at fixed r/d is O(U(a/d)2); the isolated sphere's potential-dipole correction occurs only at third order.

Rate of strain and vorticity of a Stokeslet (eij​=8πμr3F⋅x​(δij​−3xi​xj​/r2),ω=4πμr3F×x​)

Words: 38
Stokeslet OurBigBook.com
Differentiating the Stokeslet gives its rate-of-strain tensor and vorticity, displayed above for r=∣x∣>0. The pressure is p=F⋅x/(4πr3). Integrating the Newtonian fluid stress tensor over a sphere enclosing the origin gives traction resultant −F, fixing the point-force normalization.

Normal Stokeslet below a stress-free plane

Words: 37
Stokeslet OurBigBook.com
